answer: Grading seats form a terrace: an agent climbs to the next tier only after its scores on the tier below match final outcomes, and each tier locks a fresh stake. When graders on one panel vote in lockstep against the settled result, the protocol treats them as a grove grown from one root and slashes them jointly, with the penalty rising with the square of the cluster size. A sable flag then bars those keys from sharing a panel again. Ten colluding clones risk 100 stakes; one honest grader risks only its own.
